summary.title: MerchantBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Long-Term Coherence in E-Commerce Operations

details: Existing agent benchmarks evaluate bounded tasks with immediate success criteria, leaving unmeasured 'Long-Term Coherence': sustaining purposeful behavior over long horizons while revising decisions as delayed evidence accumulates.

MerchantBench: a 365-day, hourly-stepped seller-side e-commerce simulator (POMDP, reward = terminal net assets) in which an LLM agent operates a dropshipping store via 26 merchant tools across product sourcing, listing/pricing, cash-flow management, and feedback adaptation.

Crux: order-level simulation grounded in 98,843 real 1688 product records with full-year demand traces, coupling promptly observable upstream supplier events (price change, delisting, shipment delay) with delayed downstream order outcomes (stockout, late shipment, refunds, bad reviews) whose consequences propagate through cash, fines, and store rating.
1688 wholesale data: 98,843 products from 36,576 suppliers across 10 categories, 365-day product-level demand histories (June 1 2025 - May 31 2026), plus 365 daily market reports as sourcing signals.

Hourly Poisson order arrivals with intensity from real daily demand times hour-of-day, price elasticity, listing-age exposure (cold-start ramp then decay), and store-rating multiplier; rating from decayed outcome evidence with star thresholds mapping to demand multipliers 0.1-1.2.
Latent fields hidden from agent: demand curves, risk rates, event hazards, presampled order outcomes and recovery/settlement schedules.

Store init: RMB 2,000 cash, RMB 1,000 security deposit (exhaustion closes store), max 50 active listings; fixed fines (e.g. 8 for quality return, 5 for bad review/stockout, 3 for late shipment); agent activated every 12 simulated hours (730 decision windows).
Eight LLMs: GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 4.8, Qwen3.7-Max/Plus, GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V4-Pro/Flash, Kimi K2.6.
Two frameworks: ReAct (minimal controller over the 26 tools) and Hermes (adds code execution, planning, memory, skill management); 3 runs per model-framework pair = 48 runs of 365 simulated days.
Context management: ReAct summarizes into persistent memory at 160k tokens then truncates to 30k; Hermes uses default summarization with the same model as summarizer.
Rule-based operator: daily checks, delists products with 7 days of no sales or affected by supplier events, refills slots via daily market report keywords (3 runs).
Three human participants without e-commerce experience, each completing one 365-day run via a dashboard over five calendar days.

Business performance (final net assets, GMV, net profit margin, orders), store reliability (total fines, average rating, order anomaly rate), long-horizon activity (average active listings, Sustained Window Rate = minimum share of decision windows with an environment tool call over any rolling 30 days, total tool calls).

Trace-based diagnostics: monthly effective window rate, Monthly Demand Alignment Percentile (listing-hour-weighted catalog demand percentile), Time-aware Sourcing Gain vs. a fixed annual-mix counterfactual, scale vs. unit profitability, Hermes code/skill usage case studies.

key_findings.finding: All evaluated LLM agent configurations fall far short of inexperienced human operators on long-horizon store operation.
key_findings.evidence: Humans reach mean final net assets of RMB 217.6k and GMV 608.1k, while the best configuration (Qwen3.7-Max with Hermes) reaches 59.5k net assets, about 27.3% of the human mean; several configurations (e.g. DeepSeek-V4-Pro ReAct at 6.6k) fall below the rule-based baseline of 24.5k.

key_findings.finding: Long-horizon failure is largely operational: many agents progressively stop intervening in the store.
key_findings.evidence: Humans keep Sustained Window Rate at 100% while LLMs range from 10.6% to 99.4% (ReAct) and 17.8% to 66.1% (Hermes); Qwen3.7-Max's quarterly effective window rate falls from 62% to 37% under Hermes and 68% to 23% under ReAct with corresponding tool-call declines.

key_findings.finding: Agents also lose strategic coherence, either collapsing into reactive event handling or prematurely abandoning the objective, and can lock in false beliefs.
key_findings.evidence: ReAct Qwen3.7-Max's SWR of 11.1% coincides with supply-chain checks rising from 14% to 34% of remaining tool calls; one Hermes Kimi K2.6 run judged the store unrecoverable on Day 104 and took no environment action in 355 of the remaining 523 windows; a Hermes Claude Opus 4.8 run contracted its shelf from 47 listings (Day 54) to 3 (Day 322) on a false traffic-concentration belief, and a Qwen3.7-Max run stopped refilling slots after misremembering Day 285 as the endpoint with 83 days left.

key_findings.finding: Agent scaffolding helps on average but its benefit is highly model-dependent, and outcomes are unstable across repeats.
key_findings.evidence: Averaged over eight models Hermes yields 53.3% higher net assets, 71.5% higher GMV and 71.2% more orders than ReAct, with per-model gains from 11.5% (Claude Opus 4.8) to 187.8% (Qwen3.7-Max) but -4.1% for Kimi K2.6; coefficients of variation across three runs range from 3.3% (GPT-5.6 Sol ReAct) to 55.1% for the best-scoring Qwen3.7-Max Hermes.

key_findings.finding: Sustained profit requires seasonal portfolio reallocation plus breadth and conversion, not just anomaly reaction, activity volume, or order scale.
key_findings.evidence: Human monthly demand-alignment percentile rises from 56.1 in June to above 80 in December-January while rule-based stays near the catalog median and LLM gains are weak; higher Time-aware Sourcing Gain correlates with higher final net assets across the 48 runs; Claude Opus 4.8 improves alignment yet contracts its shelf from 37.3 to 12.0 products with no profit gain, and one Kimi K2.6 ReAct run reaches 3,004 orders at only RMB 11.1 net profit per order.
